top_story_title: Cisco moves to distrust eight eMudhra intermediate CAs after their private keys proved brute-forceable
top_story_summary: Cisco has published an emergency informational advisory covering a compromise of Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra, uncovered between October 17 and October 20, 2026. According to the advisory, a security researcher demonstrated that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken by an error in the April 2025 Key Generation Ceremony, to the point that anyone can brute-force the private keys within seconds. Cisco points to its own eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise material and a Cisco Talos blog post; Splunk products are handled in a separate advisory.
top_actions: Open the Cisco advisory and build the affected-product list from it directly; Cisco states products not listed are not affected, so do not scope by product family or guesswork.

Inventory every certificate in the network estate whose chain includes an eMudhra root or intermediate - device identity certificates, VPN server and client certificates, EAP-TLS/802.1X, management HTTPS, TLS syslog - and reissue from a different CA.

Remove or explicitly distrust the eMudhra roots and intermediates in the trust stores of firewalls, VPN gateways, wireless controllers and management platforms, following the per-product steps in the advisory; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release where a code change is required.
Revoke any TLS-inspection bypass, certificate pin or allow-list entry that references an eMudhra issuer.
Rotate admin credentials, API keys and session tokens that traversed TLS paths validated against these CAs, on the assumption a forged certificate could have intercepted them.
executive_summary: Cisco has issued an emergency informational advisory to distrust eight eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys can be brute-forced in seconds; scope comes from the advisory's product list, and no fixed release is stated in the source.
This is a certificate-trust event, so the exposure is machine-in-the-middle against TLS the device already trusts: inspection, VPN peer and client validation, EAP-TLS and HTTPS management planes.

Barracuda attributes the breach of its cloud environment to a stolen cloud access key used with the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework - vendor-side, with no customer appliance vulnerability claimed.

Quiet cycle otherwise: no new network device CVE, no KEV addition, and two collected items (an AI-driven espionage campaign with no device named, and N-able N-central RMM patches) fall outside network infrastructure.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Build the affected-product list from the Cisco advisory itself; Cisco's review indicates products not listed are unaffected, and the advisory is being updated, so re-check it rather than scoping once.

**Cisco** — Inventory certificates whose chain includes an eMudhra root or intermediate: device identity certificates, VPN server and client certificates, EAP-TLS/802.1X, management HTTPS, TLS syslog and any cloud-management enrolment.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Cisco issued an emergency advisory to distrust eight eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys can be brute-forced in seconds, breaking certificate trust on affected products.

headlines.title: Barracuda links cloud breach to ARTEX AI-powered cyberattack
headlines.summary: Barracuda says its cloud environment was breached using a stolen cloud access key and the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework.
